operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: "Year", "Title", "Company_name", "Group_Equity_Shareholding" — must be double-quoted verbatim; column lookup case-insensitive.

FK child columns book_club_id/movie_id are declared TEXT but reference INT parents (book_club.book_club_id, movie.movie_id): storage class contradicts declared type; sqlite affinity will coerce '1'->1 on insert.
FK child values are text-stored integers ('1','2','3','5','6'); parent PKs are integer storage — join works via affinity but literal typing differs.
culture_company.book_club_id has 5 distinct over 6 rows (one duplicate) and movie_id 6 distinct — FK child not unique, fine.
All tables tiny (12/10/6 rows); no huge-table sampling needed, but read_schema must still handle max_rows_per_table path.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints anywhere; only PKs. So drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op except PKs.
book_club.Year and movie.Year are INT with 2-3 distinct values (1989/1990, 1999/2000/2001) — declared INT dispatches to Number, not Date; year-like semantics lost.

Group_Equity_Shareholding REAL values include 100.0, 18.77 — Number fuzzer with scale from 'real' (no args) => scale 0, so fresh draws are integers in [-1,1] unless perturbed; original floats only via element reuse.
Budget_million REAL with values 4.0..41.3; Gross_worldwide INT up to 106371651 — Number full-range for INT is [-1,1] (scale 0), so fresh draws are tiny vs originals.
Result values contain brackets/spaces: 'Won [A ]', 'Won [B ]' — String fuzzer will contaminate with random chars; no format preserved.
Book_Title sample 'Whoӳ Next' contains a non-ASCII char (Cyrillic-ish) — String CHARSET is ASCII-only, so fresh strings won't reproduce it.
Category/Type/Incorporated_in are low-cardinality enums (3/3/2 distinct) but declared TEXT => String fuzzer, no enum awareness.
operator_ts_expectations: book_club_id, movie_id, Year, Gross_worldwide: Number fuzzer, scale 0 (INT), full range [-1,1]; fresh draws are -1/0/1-ish, wildly off from 1..12 / 1989..2001 / 30471..106371651.
Budget_million, Group_Equity_Shareholding: Number fuzzer, REAL with no (a,b) args => scale 0, so fresh draws integers in [-1,1]; only element reuse (5 originals) gives plausible floats.
Author_or_Editor, Book_Title, Publisher, Director, Company_name, Title: String fuzzer length 20, CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9(); fresh values are random gibberish, not names — FN risk on LIKE/name predicates.

Category, Type, Incorporated_in, Result: String fuzzer; enum values like 'Corporate','Won [A ]' only appear via 5-element reuse; fresh draws are random strings — misses equality/IN predicates on these enums (FN).

FK child book_club_id/movie_id: fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws from parent's FINAL filtered PK values (integers 1..12 / 1..10) with replacement, so child gets ints while declared TEXT — affinity coerces, join still works; but child may reference parent rows that were PK-deduped away? No: parent PKs are unique so all survive.

PKs book_club_id/movie_id/Company_name: single-column PK => max_l0 = inf, so fresh draws never capped; Company_name (TEXT PK) gets random strings, likely unique, so sample_fresh_primary_keys rarely drops.
No NOT NULL/CHECK/UNIQUE => write_instance_sqlite almost never fails a row; rows_ok ~= requested size.
Year columns: Number fuzzer produces -1/0/1, so queries like 'Year = 1999' or 'Year > 1990' will match nothing or everything — classic FN from implausible values.
Gross_worldwide: Number scale 0 => fresh draws in [-1,1]; comparisons like 'Gross_worldwide > 1000000' return empty — FN.
Group_Equity_Shareholding: fresh draws in [-1,1] but originals 18.77..100; predicates '> 50' empty — FN; '= 100' only via element reuse.

Low-cardinality enums (Category 3, Type 3, Incorporated_in 2): String fuzzer with p=0.2 fresh means ~80% element reuse, so enum values DO appear often — but contamination (0.5) mangles them, causing FP on equality.

Ties/duplicates: original has duplicate book_club_id in culture_company (5 distinct/6 rows); TS drops unique-column duplicates only, not FK duplicates, so ties preserved — but GROUP BY/COUNT ties may differ from original distribution.
